segments.he: רבינו ז"ל שבכל מקום ששני חסידי ברסלב הולכים ביחד ומדברים זה עם זה צריך לילך אחריהם סופר ולכתוב כל דיבור היוצא מפיהם כמו המנהג אצל המלכים ואנשים גדולים שהולך אחריהם סופר לכתוב כל היוצא מפיהם (כי הלא אין מדברים דברי הבל אלא חכמות כן כשאנ"ש הולכים ביחד אינם מדברים שטותים אלא חכמות אמיתיות מענין התכלית).
segments.en: Reb Avraham's disciples in Uman told me that Reb Avraham related to them [the elders of our fellowship] that the disciples of Moharan'as so cherished and loved Eretz Yisroel that when a letter came to them from Eretz Yisroel they would cherish even the postage stamp very much — that it had merited to be in Eretz Yisroel — and they would store it with their tallis and tefillin, saying: "Eretz Yisroel is tefillin and tefillin are also tefillin — so they should be kept together." And Reb Avraham himself — when he traveled for Rosh HaShanah, he would take with him a bottle of wine. And for every drink he drank in the Diaspora he would drip a drop from the wine he had brought from Eretz Yisroel into the cup — so that his drink would receive the holiness of Eretz Yisroel. And the bottle of wine was very precious to him and he was very sparing with it — only a single drop into each drink — so it would last through all the time he was in the Diaspora. Once Reb Avraham spoke with our fellowship about the holiness of Eretz Yisroel and said: "Do you think I am only saying that there are G-d-fearing people there and Eretz Yisroel helps them? There are also free-thinkers there — and Eretz Yisroel helps them too [that they are not as they were in the Diaspora]." And once one of our fellowship asked Reb Avraham whether he should travel to Eretz Yisroel. Reb Avraham certainly agreed [for he greatly encouraged our fellowship to travel to Eretz Yisroel and said every Jewish man should go to Eretz Yisroel]. And the man replied: "How can one travel away from the Rebbe?" Reb Avraham answered: "If it is your view that traveling to Eretz Yisroel means traveling away from the Rebbe — then you should indeed not go. But for me, when I travel to Eretz Yisroel I travel toward the Rebbe. [For the Tzaddik's primary place is in Eretz Yisroel — and Rabbainu said explicitly: 'My place is only in Eretz Yisroel — and for now I am pasturing in Breslov.'] And there is much more to tell of Reb Avraham on the matter of Eretz Yisroel." And Reb Avraham said that Eretz Yisroel is like a vessel of water placed on a fire — at first it seems clear, but when heated one sees it is full of sand. And the sand is poured off and it becomes clear again — until it becomes truly entirely clean. So it is with a Tzaddik and Eretz Yisroel: before coming to Eretz Yisroel it seems he is already a decent person — but when he comes, the truth is shown that he is not yet clean. And Eretz Yisroel gradually purifies him until he becomes truly clean.
